title.en: Fuel, freshness, and spotting hidden adulterants

text.en: Eating well isn't just about taste—athletes need extra carbohydrates and hydration, and every family needs to recognise FSSAI/AGMARK labels and detect food adulteration.

Good nutrition requires thoughtful meal planning based on age, gender, activity, seasonal availability, and affordability (e.g., groundnuts give similar nutrients to expensive cashews).
Human taste has five sensations: sweet, salt, bitter, sour, and umami (savoury, like MSG). Texture and temperature also shape food acceptance.
Sportspersons need high energy—primarily from carbohydrates—plus adequate hydration (cool water, coconut water, thin shakes). Excess protein supplements can strain kidneys and bones.
Food quality is certified by marks like FSSAI, AGMARK, and ISI. Spoilage is caused by microbial load and enzymes, and is slowed by heat, cold, drying, or preservatives.
Food adulteration is intentionally adding inferior substances or removing vital components for profit. Under the Food Safety and Standards Act (2006), it is illegal and dangerous.
Simple home tests detect adulterants: pure milk leaves a white trail on a vertical surface (watered milk flows fast); iodine turns starch-adulterated milk blue; HCl turns metanil yellow in dal pink; cotton tests malachite green on peas.
Smart meal planning balances nutrition, age, activity, and budget—local seasonal foods are best.
Athletes rely mainly on carbohydrates for energy and cool fluids for hydration.
Look for FSSAI, AGMARK, and ISI quality marks when buying packaged foods.
Food preservation slows spoilage by removing moisture, cooling, heating, or adding safe preservatives.
Food adulteration lowers quality for profit and harms health—especially in children and pregnant women.
Wash fruits and vegetables thoroughly under running water to reduce pesticide residues.

problem.en: How can you test at home whether arhar dal has been adulterated with metanil yellow?

text.en: Extract the colour from a sample of dal using lukewarm water.

why.en: Water-soluble dye dissolves into the liquid.

text.en: Add a few drops of HCl (hydrochloric acid): if it turns pink, metanil yellow is present.

why.en: Metanil yellow reacts with acid to give a distinct pink colour.

prompt.en: Explain what food adulteration is, name two quality marks, and describe one home adulteration test.

requiredIdeas.en: Food adulteration is intentionally adding inferior substances or removing vital nutrients
Quality marks include FSSAI, AGMARK, and ISI
Tests include iodine for starch in milk, white trail for water in milk, or HCl for metanil yellow in dal

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking expensive foods like cashews are always more nutritious than affordable foods like groundnuts

points.en: Meal planning considers age, activity, budget, and the five tastes (including umami).
Sportspersons need carbohydrate-rich energy and steady hydration.
FSSAI, AGMARK, and ISI marks certify food safety and quality.
Simple tests detect water/starch in milk, metanil yellow in dal, and malachite green in vegetables.
